purpose: Code points that make text lie about itself, replayed through both implementations that guard against them: the runtime refuses them in a publication document (crates/encastra-publish/src/bundle.rs has_control_characters) and the editor strips them from a permission prompt (apps/desktop/src/safe-text.ts forDisplay). The two lists were maintained separately and had drifted — one knew about U+FFF9, the other about nothing past U+2069. Whatever is listed as refused here must be refused by the runtime and removed by the editor; whatever is listed as allowed must pass both untouched. One deliberate difference: the allowed list describes text in a document, and the editor's prompt additionally removes newline, carriage return and tab, because a folder path with a line break in it reads as two things. The editor's test encodes exactly that difference and nothing wider.

refused.why: zero-width space: two names look identical
byte-order mark used as a zero-width no-break space
inhibit symmetric swapping: deprecated, still honoured by some renderers
Arabic letter mark: a bidi format character that is not a control
Mongolian vowel separator: formerly a space, now a format character
line separator: a second line nobody sees in a list

allowed.why: accented letters and an em dash are text, not structure
newlines are the ordinary shape of a changelog
tab and carriage return are kept with newline
right-to-left script is not a right-to-left override
